ds: Money or value transfer services and mobile money wallets move funds quickly across borders, often to cash-based endpoints. Offenders use them to send scam proceeds, structure payments through many senders and receivers, and operate unlicensed or complicit agents. Cyber-enabled aspects include compromised wallets, SIM swaps and automated account farms.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Money or Value Transfer Services (2016)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Prepaid Cards, Mobile Payments and Internet-Based Payment Services (2013)
FATF, Recommendation 16 and Interpretive Note on payment transparency

rat: Mobile money and remittance with agent cash endpoints and SIM-swap abuse.

ind.n: Many senders paying one beneficiary or many beneficiaries paid by one sender
ind.cx: Fan-in or fan-out structures with no family or business link.
ind.fp: Diaspora family support or charity collection.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Transfers just under identification or reporting thresholds
ind.cx: Repeated sends sized to avoid additional checks.
ind.ds: Repeated transfers, remittances or card/wallet loads kept just below an identification, record-keeping or travel-rule threshold.
ind.cn: Non-cash transfers or loads just below identification or reporting thresholds

ind.n: Sender profile does not match volume or purpose
ind.cx: Low-income or newly joined sender moves large sums with vague purpose.
ind.ds: Turnover or volumes materially exceed what the customer's declared occupation, income, age or circumstances would support.
ind.cn: Account activity inconsistent with declared occupation or income

ind.n: Wallet SIM swap followed by outbound transfers
ind.cx: Number is ported or SIM replaced, then funds drained to new payees.
ind.ds: Mobile number is ported or SIM replaced shortly before one-time-passcode-protected actions or outbound transfers.
ind.cn: SIM swap or number port before transfers

ind.n: Agent with unusual cash volumes or splitting behaviour
ind.cx: Agent location processes volumes far above peers, with suspicious customer splitting.
ind.ds: Agent location processes volumes far above peers, with suspicious customer splitting.

ind.n: Beneficiary account in high-risk or uncooperative jurisdiction
ind.cx: Receiving corridors are known for weak controls or sanctions risk.
ind.ds: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
ind.cn: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls

ind.n: Same device or phone used by many senders
ind.cx: Single device initiates transfers for multiple apparent customers.
ind.ds: The same device fingerprint, IP, phone, email or address appears across many applications, claims or apparent customers.
ind.cn: Shared device, contact or address data across many applicants or senders

ind.n: Rapid wallet-to-wallet hops then cash-out at agent
ind.cx: Value passes through several mobile wallets within hours before cash-out.
ind.ds: Stored value or funds move quickly between wallets or cards and are then cashed out.
ind.cn: Rapid stored-value or wallet hops then cash-out

ind.n: Missing or inconsistent originator and beneficiary information
ind.cx: Payment messages incomplete, inconsistent or use placeholder data.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
ind.cn: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information

ind.cx: Individuals operate collection points or chat-app based services with no licence.
ind.ds: Individuals operate collection points or chat-app based services with no licence.

ctl.ds: Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Collects, validates and transmits required originator and beneficiary information with virtual asset transfers and holds or blocks transfers where counterparty data is missing or unreliable. It brings wire-like transparency to virtual asset payments.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
